# Pain / Opportunity Analysis — POA-001: Quantifying the Bengali Edition Gap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | POA-001 |
| Flow Step | 06 — Quantify pain and opportunity (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | PA-001 (Product Analyst) |
| Upstream inputs | IB-001 v1.0, IOH-001 v1.0, PS-001 v3.0, ICP-001 v3.0, RF-001/H-JM-001 v1.0 |
| Reviewers this run | PM-001 (independent review, may return), CFO-001 / FPA-001 (Finance) |
| Version | 1.0 |
| **Analytics data used** | **None. No product exists; no event stream, no CRM, no billing system, no web research in this run. Participants interviewed upstream: 0 (RF-001).** |
| Method | Bottom-up decomposition; conditional-probability population cascade; expected-utility model of buyer inaction; scenario arithmetic against IOH-001's break-even. All parameters are explicitly labelled ESTIMATE with method stated inline. |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** on the analytical structure and on the three findings in §0; **Low** on every magnitude |
| Evidence quality | **Low** |
| Gate criteria ("opportunity is large enough or strategically important enough to test") | **CONDITIONALLY MET — via redefinition, not as currently scoped.** See §7 Decision. Step 06's loop condition ("stop or redefine if impact is insufficient") is invoked in the **redefine** branch. |

---

## 0. The three findings, up front

**F-1 — The beachhead as strictly defined by ICP-001 is arithmetically too small to reach break-even, and is unknown to within a factor of ~20.** ICP-001's four hard filters are *negatively correlated with each other*, not independent. Multiplying them conditionally yields a central estimate of **~113 addressable organizations worldwide** (plausible range 18–430) against an unconditional-multiplication estimate of ~353. Reaching IOH-001's operational break-even (~60 titles/year) from 113 organizations requires converting **~44% of the entire global addressable population every year, forever.** That is not a demand assumption anyone should carry into Step 07. (§3)

**F-2 — Buyer pain severity, measured in cash, is approximately zero — and that is the single most important number in this analysis.** Non-consumption costs the buyer nothing in cash. Nothing breaks. No system goes down. There is no leaking bucket. Willingness to pay is therefore **not** anchored to the value of a Bengali edition (which PS-001's P2 says the buyer cannot even compute); it is anchored to (a) the size of a pre-ringfenced localization budget line and (b) the price of *avoiding a reputational downside*. Both are bounded and both are measurable — but neither scales with the reader population, which invalidates every "250M Bengali speakers" framing as a pricing input. (§4)

**F-3 — P2 (unquantifiable return) and P4 (no route to reader), jointly ~45% of PS-001's hypothesized blockage, are solved by the *same* filter — and only there.** Reader evidence requires channel telemetry. Only a buyer who owns the channel *has* telemetry. Therefore PM-001's D-005 (restrict to channel-owning buyers) is more defensible than PM-001 argued: it is not merely MVP scope protection, it is the **only configuration in which we can measure the outcome we are selling.** But F-1 says that same filter shrinks the market below viability. This is the central tension the discovery budget must resolve, and §7 resolves it by re-grading F4 into a two-tier offer rather than a binary filter. (§5)

---

## 1. Scope, and what "quantify" can honestly mean here

Step 06 asks for frequency, severity, affected users, and measurable business impact. With n=0 participants (RF-001) and no analytics, I cannot *measure* any of these. What I can do — and what this artifact is — is build the **quantitative model into which discovery evidence will be poured**, expose which single parameters the conclusion is sensitive to, and rank the $8,000 discovery budget by uncertainty reduction per dollar (§6).

Per my permissions, no figure below is presented as FACT. Downstream artifacts (Steps 07, 10, 11, 13, 16) must cite POA-001 as **"modelled estimate, unvalidated; parameter sensitivities in POA-001 §3.3."**

```
Required Integration:
Tool: Web research + browser automation (grant databases, NGO annual reports and
  programme pages, IATI/OECD-DAC aid activity data, foundation 990s/charity registers)
Capability: Count Western-HQ mission-driven organizations with a named, funded Bangladesh
  or West Bengal programme, and cross-reference which of those list a country office or
  local implementing partner
Why Needed: The incidence rates in §3 (F2 base rate, and the two conditional
  probabilities P(no local capacity | mandate) and P(owns channel | no local capacity))
  are the parameters the entire go/no-go turns on. My central estimate and my low estimate
  differ by 6×, and the low estimate kills the business outright. This is a desk-research
  countable, not an interview finding — it is the cheapest decisive fact available to us.
Alternative: Built the cascade as an explicit parameterized model with stated ranges and a
  sensitivity table (§3.3) so that closing these three parameters immediately updates the
  verdict. All population figures labelled ESTIMATE.
Human Escalation: Fund ~$400–600 of human desk research (or connect web search) to count
  the F2∩F3 population directly from public programme listings. I am recommending in §6
  that this displace part of the $1,500 pilot-title spend in IOH-001 §3.4 and run FIRST.
```

```
Required Integration:
Tool: CRM (read/write) and analytics platform
Capability: Structured tracking of the discovery/deal funnel from first contact to invoice
Why Needed: Step 59 will ask me to analyze a funnel. At the volumes modelled in §5, that
  funnel will carry ~10–80 deals per year — statistically un-analyzable as a funnel (§8).
  Without a per-deal ledger captured from the very first outreach, we will reach Step 59
  with anecdotes and no attributable drop-off data.
Alternative: Specified a minimal 14-field Deal Ledger schema in §8 that can be maintained
  in a spreadsheet from Step 05 onward, and which forward-maps cleanly into the Step 24
  Analytics Tracking Plan.
Human Escalation: Stand up any structured store (a sheet is sufficient) before the first
  discovery conversation. Retroactive reconstruction of an abandonment funnel is not
  possible.
```
